totals.note: Row counts of this list, not downloads. Three registries, three populations, never added.

window_rule: 30-day and cumulative are different windows over the same packages. They are carried as separate fields and are never added to each other. Neither is a count of people: mirrors, CI and crawlers are inside both.
state_rule: READ: every counter in the fan-out answered. PARTIAL: some answered and the value is a lower bound over those, with covered/attempted on the row. UNCHECKABLE: a source exists and none of it answered; value null, never 0. UNMEASURED: no source exists.

downloads_30d.kind: third-party counter (includes mirror and automated traffic)
downloads_30d.method: sum of pepy.tech's daily-by-version series over the 30 complete UTC days
downloads_30d.reason: pypi 30-day: 396 of 397 counters answered; the value is a lower bound over those 396, not a total over 397

downloads_all_time.kind: third-party counter (includes mirror and automated traffic)
downloads_all_time.reason: pypi cumulative: 396 of 397 counters answered; the value is a lower bound over those 396, not a total over 397

cross_check.note: Two third-party counters over the same registry, and they do not agree. On 2026-09-22 pepy.tech's daily series ran about 2.7x pypistats' last_month on every package sampled. The likeliest reason is that they treat mirror and automated traffic differently, but neither publishes enough to settle it here, so this is recorded as an open divergence and not resolved by picking one. The figure published above is pepy's, the larger of the two, and it is labelled gross precisely because a number that includes mirrors is not a number of people. Anyone quoting it should quote this ratio beside it.

downloads_30d.kind: third-party counter (includes mirror and automated traffic)
downloads_30d.method: api.npmjs.org point/last-month, bulk where the registry allows it

downloads_all_time.window: cumulative, all time (every package answered inside npm's 18-month range window, so the window provably covers its whole life)
downloads_all_time.kind: third-party counter (includes mirror and automated traffic)
downloads_all_time.method: sum of the daily range series
downloads_all_time.proven_note: npm's range endpoint serves at most the last 18 months. For the 324 packages whose first counted download falls strictly inside that window the sum IS the all-time total; for the rest it is a lower bound.
